message.reasoning:
We need to fix compilation errors. The errors are about missing Mockito imports. The test uses Mockito annotations but we can remove them and avoid needing Mockito. The test only needs mock objects for ValidationContext, JsonNode etc. We can replace them with simple stubs or nulls. Since JsonSchema constructor expects ValidationContext, JsonNode etc. We can pass null for those parameters; but the code uses reflection to set dynamicAnchor field. In createJsonSchema we pass validationContext (which was a mock) and dummySchemaNode etc. We can just instantiate a dummy ValidationContext implementation or use null. However the constructor may require non-null? Not sure. Safer to create simple stub classes implementing interfaces? ValidationContext is a class, not interface. Let's check typical library: com.networknt.schema.ValidationContext is a class. It may have a default constructor? Probably it has a constructor requiring parameters. But we can avoid using it by passing null for ValidationContext and dummySchemaNode as null. The createJsonSchema method uses reflection to call private constructor with parameters: ValidationContext, String, URI, JsonNode, JsonSchema, boolean. It passes validationContext (mock), "dummySchemaPath", null, dummySchemaNode, null, false. If we set validationContext to null and dummySchemaNode to null, it should still work as long as constructor doesn't validate null. Usually private constructor may just assign fields; may not check null. So we can remove Mockito and just use null.

Thus modify test class: remove Mockito imports and annotations. Remove @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class). Remove @Mock fields. Instead define private ValidationContext validationContext = null; private JsonNode schemaNode = null; private JsonNode dummySchemaNode = null; Or just not declare them and use null directly.

Simplify: In createJsonSchema, use null for validationContext and dummySchemaNode.

Also remove unused imports.

Also the test uses JsonSchema.from method signature: from(ValidationContext, String, URI, JsonNode, JsonSchema, boolean). In code they pass validationContext (null) etc. That's fine.

Thus final code will compile without Mockito.

Let's rewrite file.

Also need to import necessary classes: JsonNode, ObjectMapper, ObjectNode, etc. No Mockito.

Remove @ExtendWith annotation.

Remove @Mock fields.

Update createJsonSchema to use null for validationContext and dummySchemaNode.

Also remove unused imports: org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension; org.mockito.*; org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith.

Let's craft final code.
